# Agent N's Hermes News — 2026-10-27

**Executive summary:** A delegation day — the issue's dominant story is official multi-agent routing, and it touches every section. Same-day explainers make it the week's most practical playbook for multi-agent setups, and it slots neatly beside the community's compounding orchestration layer (**[verso](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49628094)**, **[Oh My Hermes](/?date=2026-10-27&category=social#item-910f505f9bd1)**). The release side is a routine canary: [**v0.22.5+canary.20261026T071310Z**](/?date=2026-10-27&category=news#item-90c18442f069) for pre-release testing continues the automated cadence — with stable **v0.22.5** (rolled out 10-24 across **CLI**, **Microsoft Store**, **Docker**, and **Hermes Cloud**) still the operative build for everyone else. Tips carry the efficiency story: the [**execute_code**](/?date=2026-10-27&category=news#item-17db82837839) walkthrough shows how programmatic tool calling collapses multi-step processes into single turns — major workflow compression — while the delegation guides are the other must-read. The social feed pairs launch anticipation with unusual candor: **@NousResearch** teased [Friday launches](/?date=2026-10-27&category=social#item-d8647ef8fd1e) and **@Teknium** confirmed a major feature landing ["literally tomorrow"](/?date=2026-10-27&category=social#item-23e8eb73bf33) — watch-items until tagged — while his [honest roadmap update](/?date=2026-10-27&category=social#item-85fa01872a55) concedes **proactive-agent** functionality is still being evaluated and the **Hermes Desktop** effort has faced leadership changes; the concrete delivery is that [new subscriptions now automatically receive a cloud instance](/?date=2026-10-27&category=social#item-8ba07ac361e5). De-dup duty, twelfth cycle running: the [**Claude Pro/Max** subscription support](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49790991) (documented on the official plugins page; **@Teknium**'s "finally here" post is ambiguous but likely refers to this — carried since 10-20), the [**Hermes Kanban** multi-agent docs](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49604068), the [**Grafana** observability stack](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49318128), the [**Kubernetes** gaps](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49977400) (no official **Helm** chart, root-at-init image, community workaround recipe — still the highest-impact deployment finding), **Almanac**, **verso**, the [~**23,000**-open-PR backlog](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49424643) and the stale [**v0.20.0**](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49159200) release line (tagged **v2026.8.3** — a versioning discrepancy worth verifying, and months old regardless) are all reference, not news. One verification flag: the [runaway-agent incident](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49916751) on headless **Debian** cites "Z.ai **GLM 5.3 Flash**," which does not match the tracker (newest GLM is **GLM-5.2**, released 2026-06-16) — treat the model ID as unverified; two SEO link-building spam items and the Hermès trademark thread were excluded. Also on the research watchlist: [**ProAS**](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-2610.18683) (arXiv **2610.18683**) on uniform credit assignment in multi-turn agentic RL — relevant to future Hermes-style agent training — and the default-bundled [**llm-wiki**](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-5ea2212b5088) skill (**v2.1.0**) for persistent research knowledge. Housekeeping: Reddit contributed nothing again. Net read: official multi-agent delegation plus automatic cloud instances for subscribers show the platform maturing at both the orchestration and delivery layers, community clients are closing the remaining platform gaps, and a candor-forward founder post sits comfortably next to Friday-launch teasers. Practical agenda: read the [**Advanced Delegation** explainers](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-679ef7221396) before your next multi-agent run and wire up **model_map**/**profile_routes**; use [**execute_code**](/?date=2026-10-27&category=news#item-17db82837839) to compress multi-step workflows; try [**hermes-anywhere**](/?date=2026-10-27&category=news#item-3f757d6bb1c2) if you need **Windows**/**Android** continuity; canary testers take [**v0.22.5+canary.20261026T071310Z**](/?date=2026-10-27&category=news#item-90c18442f069); everyone else stay on stable **v0.22.5**; hit the [**Kubernetes** recipe](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49977400) if you're deploying on **K8s**; treat the "**GLM 5.3 Flash**" ID and the **v0.20.0** versioning discrepancy as unverified; and watch for Friday's launches and the "literally tomorrow" feature — filing **Pro/Max**, **Kanban**, **Grafana**, **Almanac**, **verso**, the **~23k** backlog, and **llm-wiki v2.1.0** as reference.

Quiet for tagged stable builds — the only shipped artifact this cycle is the routine pre-release **[Hermes Agent v0.22.5+canary.20261026T071310Z](/?date=2026-10-27&category=news#item-90c18442f069)**, published on GitHub for pre-release testing. Stable **v0.22.5** (GA 10-24, rolled out simultaneously across **CLI**, **Microsoft Store**, **Docker**, and **Hermes Cloud**) remains the operative build — run stable wherever you run Hermes.

The forward-looking signal comes from social: **@NousResearch** teased [upcoming releases on **Friday**](/?date=2026-10-27&category=social#item-d8647ef8fd1e), and **@Teknium** confirmed a major feature is launching ["literally tomorrow"](/?date=2026-10-27&category=social#item-23e8eb73bf33). ## Community

- **[hermes-anywhere](/?date=2026-10-27&category=news#item-3f757d6bb1c2)** (the top story): a new community-built **Flutter** and **Cupertino** client for **Hermes Agent**, enabling cross-platform access and session continuity across **Windows** and **Android**. If you move between desktop and mobile and want your sessions to follow, this is the project to try.
- **[Oh My Hermes (OMH)](/?date=2026-10-27&category=social#item-910f505f9bd1)**: **@rlaope** continues pushing **OMH** as an operating layer for **Hermes Agent**, this cycle with significant hardware benchmarking work — a continuation of the line we've tracked since **Zeus 4.0.0**.
- **[verso](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49628094)**: the open-source orchestrator for users who'd rather not touch a CLI remains in active circulation with founder amplification from **@Teknium** boosting visibility — still reference, but the amplification is new.
- **[Almanac](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49511007)** (**YC S26**): the company-knowledge/context startup stays on the ecosystem radar.
- **@NousResearch** community-building: hosting an [anti-slop hackathon](/?date=2026-10-27&category=social#item-0eee056c3dc7) in **NYC** at **Pangram HQ**, and giving positive feedback to user-created agents — the ecosystem-first posture continues.

- **Advanced Delegation — the must-read of the cycle.** First-party documentation now covers the full delegation stack: the official [**Advanced Delegation** plugin](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-679ef7221396) routes each subagent to a different model or profile via **model_map** (model routes) and **profile_routes** (profile modes); the core [**delegate_task** primitive](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-f72edb8c3a45) spawns fresh, isolated child contexts with parallelism limits and inherited provider settings; and [**delegation.model**](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-a441ad5b5c1c) enables per-subagent model selection. Multiple same-day guides mean you can go from zero to a routed multi-agent setup in one sitting. Read before your next multi-agent run.
- **[execute_code](/?date=2026-10-27&category=news#item-17db82837839) for workflow compression.** A walkthrough of the built-in **execute_code** tool shows how programmatic tool calling collapses multi-step processes into single turns — a major efficiency win for anyone chaining tools manually today.
- **[Claude Pro/Max subscription support](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49790991).** Now documented on the official plugins page: subscribers can connect existing **Claude Pro/Max** plans to the agent. **@Teknium** posted that a long-requested feature is ["finally here"](/?date=2026-10-27&category=social#item-a9a5214e7550) — the post is ambiguous, but likely refers to this integration. Note: this capability has been carried in our coverage since 10-20, so treat today's framing as re-documentation, not a fresh launch.
- **[Kubernetes deployment gaps](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49977400) — still the highest-impact practical finding.** Two issues persist: no official **Helm** chart, and a container image requiring **root** at init. A [community containerization recipe](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-50131496) works around the latter. If you're deploying on **K8s**, start there.
- **[Grafana observability stack](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49318128).** The **Grafana**-based stack for monitoring Hermes agents shipped this cycle's documentation — useful if you're running agents in production.
- Verification notes for model-focused readers: the [runaway-agent incident](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49916751) on headless **Debian** cites "Z.ai **GLM 5.3 Flash**," which does not match the model tracker (newest tracked GLM is **GLM-5.2**, released 2026-06-16) — treat the model ID as unverified before citing the incident. The [**v0.20.0**](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49159200) release note (tagged **v2026.8.3**) carries a versioning discrepancy worth verifying and is months-old coverage of an existing release, not a fresh launch. On the research watchlist: [**ProAS**](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-2610.18683) (arXiv **2610.18683**) tackles uniform credit assignment in multi-turn agentic RL — relevant to future Hermes-style agent training — and the default-bundled [**llm-wiki**](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-5ea2212b5088) skill (**v2.1.0**) provides persistent research knowledge.

top_items.title: Hermes Advanced Delegation: Model Routes and Profile Routes Explained
top_items.content:
Hermes advanced delegation is a new official plugin from Nous Research that lets your Hermes Agent pick the right model, or the right profile, for every subagent it spawns. Out of the box, every subagent runs on one model. With Advanced Delegation you give Hermes a short menu instead — a fast route, a deep route, a local route, or a whole team of profiles — and it chooses per task. In this guide I’ll walk you through what it does, how to install it, how to set it up in two minutes and the gotchas to watch for.

Key takeaways

- Adds two delegation modes: model routes ( `model_map`) and profile routes ( `profile_routes`).

- Install with `hermes plugins install advanced-delegation`. Needs Hermes 0.22.5 or newer.

- Set it up with `hermes delegation config`; switch modes in chat with `/delegation`.

- Only route names and descriptions reach the model — never your keys. Claim a free strategy session to plan your agent setup.

## What is Hermes advanced delegation?

Hermes already ships with subagents. When a job is big, the agent calls its `delegate_task` tool and spawns child agents that work in parallel with a fresh context, then hand back a summary. (I cover the basics in my guide to Hermes Agent subagents.)

The catch is that, by default, every one of those subagents runs on the same model. Either they all inherit your main model, or they all run on the single `delegation.model` you pinned in config. There’s no way to say “use a cheap model for this lookup and a strong one for that bug”.

The advanced-delegation plugin fixes that. It’s part of the Hermes Official Plugins from Nous Research (version 1.0.0, author NousResearch) and adds two extra modes next to the built-in default. Only one mode is active at a time.

Mode
`delegation.backend`
What the agent gets

Default (built into Hermes)
`default`
Every subagent runs on `delegation.model` / `delegation.provider`, otherwise the parent’s model

Model routes
`model_map`
A named model route per task, from a list you define (for example fast, deep, local)

Profile routes
`profile_routes`
The subagent runs as one of your Hermes profiles, with that profile’s own model, credentials, skills and SOUL.md

Hermes core still handles the whole subagent lifecycle — spawning, isolation, depth and concurrency limits, background runs and results. The plugin only answers one question: which route does this task take?

## Mode 1: model routes (model_map)

Model routes are a menu of models with a name and a one-line description each. The agent reads the names and descriptions and picks one per task. A typical setup has three:

- fast — cheap and quick: lookups, summaries, simple edits.

- deep — slow and careful: hard debugging and design work, with a higher reasoning effort.

- local — private: runs on your own machine through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Here’s what that looks like in `config.yaml`, based on the official README:

```
delegation:
  backend: model_map
  backends:
    model_map:
      options:
        - name: fast
          description: "Cheap and quick: lookups, summaries, simple edits."
          provider: openrouter
          model: google/gemini-3-flash-preview
        - name: deep
          description: "Slow and careful: hard debugging and design work."
          provider: anthropic
          model: claude-opus-5
          reasoning_effort: high
        - name: local
          description: "Private: runs on this machine."
          base_url: http://localhost:8080/v1
          model: qwen3-coder
      default: fast
```

Each route needs a `name`, a `description`, a `model` and a `provider` or `base_url`. You can also set `reasoning_effort`, a `service_tier` (normal, fast or ultrafast), `fallback_providers`, `api_key` and `api_mode`. The README recommends `provider:` over `api_key:`, because an API key in `config.yaml` is stored in plain text, while provider credentials stay in `.env` or `auth.json`.

A task that doesn’t pick a route runs on the `default` you set. If you set no default, it runs on the parent’s own model.

## Mode 2: profile routes (profile_routes)

Profile routes go a step further. Instead of a model, each route is one of your Hermes profiles. When the agent picks a profile, the subagent runs exactly as if you’d started `hermes -p <profile>` for that task — with that profile’s own model, credentials, skills and SOUL.md.

That means you can build a small team: a coder profile that writes and tests code, a researcher profile tuned for long web research, and so on. Your main agent hands each job to the right specialist.

```
delegation:
  backend: profile_routes
  backends:
    profile_routes:
      profiles:
        - name: coder
          description: Writes and refactors code; runs tests.
        - name: researcher
          description: Web research and long-form summaries.
      default: coder
```

The list is also an allowlist: profiles you don’t list can never be picked, and a listed name with no matching profile on disk is refused with a pointer to `hermes profile list`.

Security note: listing a profile lets this profile’s subagents use that profile’s credentials, credential pool, SOUL.md and terminal policy. Only list profiles whose keys and terminal access you’re happy for this agent to use.

## How to install the plugin

You need Hermes 0.22.5 or newer — the first release with pluggable delegation providers. Hermes 0.22.0 to 0.22.4 refuses to install or enable it. Run `hermes update` first if you’re on an older build.

- Command line: `hermes plugins install advanced-delegation` (installs the reviewed version from the Hermes plugin catalog).

- Desktop app: go to Settings → Model → Subagents → Install plugin. The button shows under the mode picker while the plugin is missing.

- Latest main branch: `hermes plugins install NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#advanced-delegation --enable`.

Plugins are installed per profile, so install and configure it in the profile that does the delegating. The target profiles for profile routes don’t need anything installed — they just have to exist and have a working model.

## Set it up with hermes delegation config

You don’t have to touch YAML. The plugin adds a guided setup:

```
hermes delegation config          # pick the mode, then edit its routes
hermes delegation config --show   # print the current mode and routes
```

- Pick the mode: Default, Model routes or Profile routes.

- Model routes opens a route editor built from `hermes model` ’s own pickers: a name, a one-line description, a provider you have credentials for (or a custom endpoint), a model, an optional reasoning effort and a speed tier if the route offers one. Each route is checked before it’s saved.

- Profile routes is a checklist of your other profiles, an optional line about each, and a default.

- Default switches back to the built-in behaviour.

Everything is written to the profile’s `config.yaml` using Hermes’s own config writer, so your comments and other settings are kept. Changes apply to new sessions.

## Switch modes in a chat with /delegation

Command
What it does

`/delegation`
Shows the current mode and a picker to switch

`/delegation model_map`
Saves model routes; takes effect from the next session (`/new`)

`/delegation profiles --now`
Saves profile routes and applies them to this chat now

`/delegation default`
Back to the built-in behaviour from the next session

Why does a switch normally wait for `/new`? Because the per-task choices the model sees are part of its tool list, and the tool list is part of the prompt cache. Changing it mid-chat makes the next request re-read the whole conversation at full price. `--now` is the opt-in when you want the new mode straight away — it costs one prompt-cache miss.

On Telegram, Discord and Slack, bare `/delegation` shows buttons; in the CLI, TUI and Desktop it uses the normal picker.

## Fail-closed: no silent switches

One thing I like about this plugin is that it never quietly runs your work on the wrong model. If the selected backend is missing or disabled, `delegate_task` returns an error naming the backend and the fix, and no subagent starts. Inside a batch, a task that can’t be routed — an unknown option, a missing profile, a speed tier the route doesn’t offer, missing credentials — is refused on its own while the other tasks still run.

Every routed result also reports its `route`: the route name plus the provider, model, reasoning effort and speed tier the subagent actually ran on. So you can always check which model did which job. To go back without the plugin, run `hermes config set delegation.backend default`.

## When should you use it?

- Cutting costs: send simple research and summaries to a fast, cheap route and keep the strong model for hard problems. Subagents usually burn most of a run’s tokens, so this is where the savings are.

- Privacy: keep sensitive tasks on a local route.

- Specialist teams: use profile routes so a coding profile, a research profile and a writing profile each do what they’re best at.

- Stay simple if you don’t need it: if one model is fine for every subagent, the built-in default is all you need.

For choosing the actual models, see my guide to the Hermes subagent model settings.

## My verdict on Hermes advanced delegation

This is the missing piece for anyone running serious multi-agent work in Hermes. You keep one planner, and every subagent lands on the right model or the right specialist profile, with your keys never exposed to the model and no silent fallbacks. If you’re on Hermes 0.22.5 or newer, install Hermes advanced delegation, set up a fast and a deep route, and watch your subagent bills drop.

## About Julian Goldie

I’m Julian Goldie — founder of Goldie Agency and the AI Profit Boardroom. I test new AI agents almost every day for 432K+ YouTube subscribers and run Hermes, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Claude and Codex side by side in my own Agent OS. Claim your free strategy session or join the AI Profit Boardroom.

## FAQ: hermes advanced delegation

### What is Hermes advanced delegation?

An official Nous Research plugin for Hermes Agent that adds two delegation modes: model routes, where the agent picks a named model per subagent, and profile routes, where a subagent runs as one of your Hermes profiles.

### How do I install the advanced-delegation plugin?

Run hermes plugins install advanced-delegation, or in the Desktop app go to Settings, Model, Subagents, Install plugin. It needs Hermes 0.22.5 or newer.

### What is the difference between model_map and profile_routes?

model_map gives the agent a list of named model routes such as fast, deep and local. profile_routes lets a subagent run as one of your Hermes profiles with its own model, credentials, skills and SOUL.md.

### Can the agent see my API keys?

No. Only the route names and one-line descriptions reach the model. Provider, model, endpoint and key fields never become tool parameters.

### Why does /delegation wait until /new?

Changing the mode changes the agent’s tool list, which is part of the prompt cache. Waiting for a new session avoids re-reading the whole chat at full price. Add –now to apply it immediately.

Every subagent runs on delegation.model / delegation.provider, otherwise the parent’s model

Model routes

model_map

A named model route per task, from a list you define (for example fast, deep, local)

Profile routes

profile_routes

The subagent runs as one of your Hermes profiles, with that profile’s own model, credentials, skills and SOUL.md

Hermes core still handles the whole subagent lifecycle — spawning, isolation, depth and concurrency limits, background runs and results. The plugin only answers one question: which route does this task take?

Mode 1: model routes (model_map)

Model routes are a menu of models with a name and a one-line description each. The agent reads the names and descriptions and picks one per task. A typical setup has three:

  • fast — cheap and quick: lookups, summaries, simple edits.
  • deep — slow and careful: hard debugging and design work, with a higher reasoning effort.
  • local — private: runs on your own machine through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Here’s what that looks like in config.yaml, based on the official README:

```

delegation:

backend: model_map

backends:

model_map:

options:

  • name: fast

description: "Cheap and quick: lookups, summaries, simple edits."

provider: openrouter

model: google/gemini-3-flash-preview

  • name: deep

description: "Slow and careful: hard debugging and design work."

provider: anthropic

model: claude-opus-5

reasoning_effort: high

  • name: local

description: "Private: runs on this machine."

base_url: http://localhost:8080/v1

model: qwen3-coder

default: fast

```

Each route needs a name, a description, a model and a provider or base_url. You can also set reasoning_effort, a service_tier (normal, fast or ultrafast), fallback_providers, api_key and api_mode. The README recommends provider: over api_key:, because an API key in config.yaml is stored in plain text, while provider credentials stay in .env or auth.json.

A task that doesn’t pick a route runs on the default you set. If you set no default, it runs on the parent’s own model.

Mode 2: profile routes (profile_routes)

Profile routes go a step further. Instead of a model, each route is one of your Hermes profiles. When the agent picks a profile, the subagent runs exactly as if you’d started hermes -p for that task — with that profile’s own model, credentials, skills and SOUL.md.

```
backend: profile_routes

backends:
```

How to install the plugin

  • Desktop app: go to Settings → Model → Subagents → Install plugin. The button shows under the mode picker while the plugin is missing.


Switch modes in a chat with /delegation

Command

What it does

/delegation

Shows the current mode and a picker to switch

/delegation model_map

Saves model routes; takes effect from the next session (/new)

Saves profile routes and applies them to this chat now

Back to the built-in behaviour from the next session

One thing I like about this plugin is that it never quietly runs your work on the wrong model.   • Privacy: keep sensitive tasks on a local route.

  • Stay simple if you don’t need it: if one model is fine for every subagent, the built-in default is all you need.

This is the missing piece for anyone running serious multi-agent work in Hermes. top_items.title: Hermes Agent Subagents: How delegate_task Spawns and Controls Them
top_items.content:
Hermes Agent subagents are real: Hermes can split a big job into smaller pieces and hand each one to a child agent that works on its own, in parallel, then reports back. It does this through a built-in tool called `delegate_task`. In the video below I show how you can watch and control subagents live. Here’s how subagents actually work, the one mistake that ruins most delegations, and when you should (and shouldn’t) use them.

Key takeaways

- Yes — Hermes spawns subagents with its built-in `delegate_task` tool.

- Each subagent starts with a completely fresh conversation; only its final summary comes back.

- Up to 10 run in parallel by default, and you can list, steer or stop them live.

- Nesting is off by default (flat delegation). Claim a free strategy session to plan your setup.

## Does Hermes Agent have subagents?

Yes. According to the official Subagent Delegation docs, the `delegate_task` tool “spawns child AIAgent instances with isolated context, inherited tool access, and their own terminal sessions”. Each child gets a fresh conversation and works independently, and only its final summary enters the parent’s context.

That last part is the point. A big research job or refactor would normally flood your main conversation with tool output. With subagents, the messy work happens somewhere else and you get a clean summary back. You don’t even have to ask — the docs say the agent delegates automatically when a task is complex enough. You can also tell it directly: “Use a subagent for this.”

## How delegate_task works

There are two ways to call it. A single task:

```
delegate_task(
    goal="Debug why tests fail",
    context="Error: assertion in test_foo.py line 42"
)
```

Or a parallel batch, where several subagents run at once:

```
delegate_task(tasks=[
    {"goal": "Research topic A", "context": "Focus on recent primary sources"},
    {"goal": "Research topic B", "context": "Compare the leading explanations"},
    {"goal": "Fix the build", "context": "Project root: /home/user/project"}
])
```

Top-level delegations run in the background. Hermes returns a handle straight away so you can keep chatting, then posts the result back as a new message when the children finish. By default a batch comes back as one consolidated message; set `delegation.independent_completions: true` if you want each result as soon as it lands.

Each subagent also gets its own terminal session and inherits the parent’s enabled toolsets, API key, provider settings and credential pool. A task can even carry an `output_schema`, so the child must return JSON in the shape you need.

## The fresh-context rule (the #1 mistake)

This is the part most people get wrong. Subagents know nothing about your conversation. They have zero knowledge of what you discussed, what tools ran or what files you looked at. The only context they get is the `goal` and `context` the parent writes into the call.

Here’s the bad versus good example straight from the docs:

```
# BAD - subagent has no idea what "the error" is
delegate_task(goal="Fix the error")

# GOOD - subagent has all context it needs
delegate_task(
    goal="Fix the TypeError in api/handlers.py",
    context="""The file api/handlers.py has a TypeError on line 47:
    'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'.
    The project is at /home/user/myproject and uses Python 3.11."""
)
```

One helpful exception: if the parent has a workspace, each subagent’s system prompt includes that project’s context files (like AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md), so it follows the repo’s rules without rediscovering them. You can also pass up to 8 images to a subagent when the job is visual.

Claim Your Free SEO Strategy Session →

## Limits: parallel, depth and iterations

Setting
Default
What it controls

`max_concurrent_children`
10
How many subagents run in parallel per batch (floor 1, no hard ceiling)

`max_spawn_depth`
1 (flat)
How deep the tree can go; children can’t delegate further at the default

`max_iterations`
250
Tool-calling turns each subagent can take

`child_timeout_seconds`
0 (no timeout)
Optional inactivity cap; a stall monitor still catches frozen children

`oneshot_max_children`
2
Total subagents in a one-shot `hermes chat -q` run

A batch bigger than the concurrency limit returns an error instead of being silently cut short. Some tools are blocked for subagents even if the parent has them: `clarify` (they can’t ask you questions), `memory` (no writes to shared memory), `send_message` and `cronjob`. Leaf subagents also can’t call `delegate_task` themselves.

## Nested subagents: the orchestrator role

By default delegation is flat: your agent spawns children, and those children can’t spawn their own. For bigger workflows, a parent can spawn an orchestrator child with `role="orchestrator"`, which can run its own workers.

This only works once you raise `delegation.max_spawn_depth` to 2 or more. And there’s a cost warning in the docs: with a depth of 3 and 3 children per level, the tree can reach 3×3×3 = 27 leaf agents running at once. Raise the depth on purpose, not by accident. You can switch nesting off entirely with `orchestrator_enabled: false`.

## Watch, steer and stop subagents live

This is what my video above focuses on. You don’t have to wait blindly for results. The parent agent can manage its own children with the same tool:

```
{"action": "list"}
{"action": "steer", "subagent_id": "sa-0-1a2b3c4d", "message": "focus on pricing instead"}
{"action": "stop",  "subagent_id": "sa-0-1a2b3c4d"}
```

- CLI: press Ctrl+T (or F6) for the live roster; s to steer, x then y to stop.

- TUI: `/agents` shows a live tree with cost and token rollups.

- Desktop: expand Subagents above the composer and use Steer or Stop.

Every subagent also writes a live log you can tail under `~/.hermes/cache/delegation/live/`. For more detail on redirecting a running child, see my Hermes subagent steering guide.

## When to use subagents (and when not to)

Use subagents for
Do it inline instead

Parallel research on several topics
A quick question with one answer

Big refactors that would flood your context
A small edit to one file

Independent tasks that don’t depend on each other
Steps where B needs A’s result first

Work that needs judgment and reasoning
Mechanical scripts (use `execute_code`)

The docs put it simply: use `delegate_task` when the subtask needs reasoning or judgment, and `execute_code` for mechanical data processing. Also remember that a background subagent doesn’t survive a Hermes restart — for work that must run no matter what, use a cron job. For running whole teams of agents, see my Hermes multi-agent guide.

## Keep costs under control

Subagents are where the tokens go. A parallel batch usually burns most of a run’s total tokens. The easy win is to keep your main agent on a strong model and run the subagents on a cheaper one — I explain exactly how in my Hermes subagent model guide. If you want a different model per task, the new Hermes advanced delegation plugin lets the agent pick from named routes.

## My verdict on Hermes Agent subagents

Subagents turn one Hermes into a small team: parallel research, clean context, live control and clear limits. Write full goals and context, start flat, and only add depth when you need it. Get that right and Hermes Agent subagents will do hours of work while you keep chatting.

top_items.title: Hermes Subagent Model: How to Choose the Model Each Subagent Runs On
top_items.content:
Your Hermes subagent model decides how smart, how fast and how expensive every child agent is. By default, Hermes subagents simply use the same model as your main agent. That’s easy, but it’s rarely the cheapest setup, because subagents are where most of your tokens go. In the video below I show subagents doing real work for me. ```

top_items.content:
The Hermes LLM wiki turns Hermes Agent into a research assistant that builds and maintains its own knowledge base: a folder of interlinked markdown pages that gets better every time you add a source. It comes as a bundled skill, llm-wiki, based on Andrej Karpathy’s LLM Wiki pattern, and it’s installed by default. In the video below I show the three layers, the three core operations and the setup. Here’s the full practical guide, from your first wiki to keeping it healthy.

Key takeaways

- The llm-wiki skill ships with Hermes (research/llm-wiki, v2.1.0, MIT).

- Your wiki is just markdown in ~/wiki (or WIKI_PATH) — no database.

- Three operations: ingest, query and lint.

- It opens as an Obsidian vault. Claim a free strategy session to plan your setup.

## What the Hermes LLM wiki is

The idea comes from Karpathy’s LLM Wiki gist, which he calls an “idea file”: instead of asking an AI to rediscover your documents every time you ask a question, you let it build a persistent wiki that compounds. Hermes turns that idea into a bundled skill. The docs list it under research as llm-wiki, version 2.1.0, MIT-licensed, for Linux, macOS and Windows, with the obsidian and arxiv skills as related skills.

The SKILL.md sets out a clear split. You curate the sources and direct the analysis. The agent summarises, cross-references, files pages and keeps everything consistent. Unlike retrieval-based search, the knowledge is compiled once and kept current, so answers get better as the wiki grows. I covered the bigger picture earlier in Hermes AI LLM wiki integration; this page is the hands-on setup.

## How to start your first wiki

Every installed skill in Hermes becomes a slash command, so you can run `/llm-wiki`. You can also just ask: “start a wiki about AI agents”, “ingest this article” or “lint my wiki”. Hermes picks the skill up when you create a wiki, add a source, ask a question the wiki can answer, run a health check or mention the wiki.

Choose where it lives with the `WIKI_PATH` environment variable, for example in `~/.hermes/.env`. If you don’t set it, the default is `~/wiki`.

```
# ~/.hermes/.env
WIKI_PATH=~/wiki
```

On the first run the agent works out the path, creates the folders, asks what the wiki is about, writes SCHEMA.md, index.md and log.md, and suggests your first sources. It’s just a directory of markdown, so you can open it in Obsidian, VS Code or any editor.

## The three layers

Layer
What it holds
Who owns it

Raw
Your original sources: articles, papers, transcripts and assets. Never edited.
You

Wiki
Summaries, entity and concept pages, comparisons and filed answers
The agent

Schema
SCHEMA.md: the rules for structure, naming and tags
You and the agent together

Karpathy’s gist describes the same split and notes the schema can be a file like CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md. In Hermes it’s SCHEMA.md. At the start of every session the agent reads SCHEMA.md, index.md and the last 20 to 30 log entries before it does anything, so it always knows the current state.

## The folder structure

```
~/wiki/
  SCHEMA.md        # rules for the wiki
  index.md         # map of every page
  log.md           # append-only history (rotated)
  raw/             # articles, papers, transcripts, assets
  entities/        # people, companies, tools
  concepts/        # ideas and methods
  comparisons/     # side-by-side analysis
  queries/         # answers worth keeping
```

Raw files carry a little frontmatter — source URL, ingest date and a sha256 hash. If you re-ingest a source that hasn’t changed, the agent skips it; if it has changed, the agent flags the drift.

## Ingest, query and lint

### Ingest

- The agent captures the source into raw/ (it can extract web pages and PDFs).

- It talks through the key takeaways with you (skipped when running on a schedule).

- It checks what already exists, then writes or updates pages, updates index.md and log.md, and reports the changes.

One source can update 5 to 15 pages. If an ingest would touch 10 or more existing pages, the agent asks first.

### Query

- It reads index.md (and searches once the wiki passes about 100 pages).

- It reads the relevant pages and writes an answer that cites them with [[wikilinks]].

- Valuable answers get filed in queries/ or comparisons/ and logged, so the wiki gets smarter from your questions.

### Lint

- Finds orphan pages, broken wikilinks and pages missing from the index.

- Checks frontmatter, stale pages (over 90 days), contradictions and low-confidence claims.

- Spots source drift, pages over about 200 lines, messy tags and a log that needs rotating (over 500 entries).

- Reports issues by severity and logs the run.

Want Hermes running your research and knowledge base for you? Claim your free strategy session →

Claim Your Free SEO Strategy Session →

## The conventions that keep it clean

- Lowercase, hyphenated filenames.

- YAML frontmatter on every page: title, created, updated, type, tags and sources, plus optional confidence, contested and contradictions.

- At least two outbound [[wikilinks]] per page.

- Provenance markers on pages built from three or more sources.

- A tag taxonomy of 10 to 20 tags.

- A page gets created when two or more sources mention something, or it’s central to one.

- Split pages that grow past about 200 lines, and move retired pages to _archive/.

## Obsidian integration and headless sync

The wiki works as an Obsidian vault out of the box: wikilinks are clickable, Graph View shows how everything connects, and the frontmatter powers Dataview queries. Set Obsidian’s attachment folder to `raw/assets/`. If you also use the obsidian skill, point `OBSIDIAN_VAULT_PATH` at the same folder as your wiki. Karpathy sums the pairing up neatly: “Obsidian is the IDE; the LLM is the program.”

If Hermes runs on a server, the skill describes syncing with Obsidian Headless. You need Node 22+ and an Obsidian Sync subscription:

```
npm install -g obsidian-headless
ob login
ob sync-create-remote --name "LLM Wiki"
ob sync-setup --vault "<vault-id>"
ob sync --continuous
```

You can run the continuous sync as a systemd user service so it keeps going after you log out. For more on pairing Hermes with Obsidian, see Hermes Obsidian.

## LLM Wiki vs RAG

LLM Wiki
RAG

How it works
Compiles sources into a maintained wiki
Searches raw documents at question time

Memory
Persistent and compounding
Rediscovers the answer each time

What you can see
Readable markdown pages you can browse and edit
Hidden chunks in a vector store

Scale
An index works up to roughly 100 sources and hundreds of pages, per Karpathy
Built for large document sets

RAG is still useful for huge document piles. For a focused research topic you return to again and again, the wiki wins because the work you put in stays done.

## Troubleshooting the Hermes LLM wiki

- The skill is missing. Bundled skills are copied into ~/.hermes/skills/ when you install and synced on `hermes update`. Restore it with `hermes skills reset llm-wiki --restore`.

- The wiki is in the wrong place. Check WIKI_PATH in ~/.hermes/.env; without it the wiki goes to ~/wiki.

- Answers ignore recent work. Make sure SCHEMA.md, index.md and log.md exist and are up to date — the agent reads them first.

- Big ingests stall. Ingests touching 10+ pages wait for your approval.

- You want a batch build. The skill mentions llm-wiki-compiler, a Node.js CLI that compiles a wiki in one pass; use the skill itself when you want the agent curating with you.

## My verdict on the Hermes LLM wiki

It’s one of the most useful skills already sitting in your Hermes install. Set WIKI_PATH, run /llm-wiki, feed it a few good sources and lint it once a week, and you end up with a knowledge base that keeps getting better instead of a pile of chats you never read again. If you research anything seriously, set up the Hermes LLM wiki today.

Yes. The wiki folder works as an Obsidian vault out of the box, with clickable wikilinks, Graph View and Dataview support.

  • Your wiki is just markdown in ~/wiki (or WIKI_PATH) — no database.
  • Three operations: ingest, query and lint.
  • It opens as an Obsidian vault. Claim a free strategy session to plan your setup.

What the Hermes LLM wiki is

The idea comes from Karpathy’s LLM Wiki gist, which he calls an “idea file”: instead of asking an AI to rediscover your documents every time you ask a question, you let it build a persistent wiki that compounds. Hermes turns that idea into a bundled skill. The docs list it under research as llm-wiki, version 2.1.0, MIT-licensed, for Linux, macOS and Windows, with the obsidian and arxiv skills as related skills.

The SKILL.md sets out a clear split. You curate the sources and direct the analysis. The agent summarises, cross-references, files pages and keeps everything consistent. Unlike retrieval-based search, the knowledge is compiled once and kept current, so answers get better as the wiki grows. I covered the bigger picture earlier in Hermes AI LLM wiki integration; this page is the hands-on setup.

How to start your first wiki

Every installed skill in Hermes becomes a slash command, so you can run /llm-wiki. You can also just ask: “start a wiki about AI agents”, “ingest this article” or “lint my wiki”. Hermes picks the skill up when you create a wiki, add a source, ask a question the wiki can answer, run a health check or mention the wiki.

Choose where it lives with the WIKI_PATH environment variable, for example in ~/.hermes/.env. If you don’t set it, the default is ~/wiki.

```

# ~/.hermes/.env

WIKI_PATH=~/wiki

```

On the first run the agent works out the path, creates the folders, asks what the wiki is about, writes SCHEMA.md, index.md and log.md, and suggests your first sources. It’s just a directory of markdown, so you can open it in Obsidian, VS Code or any editor.

The three layers

Layer

What it holds

Who owns it

Raw

Your original sources: articles, papers, transcripts and assets. Never edited.

You

Wiki

Summaries, entity and concept pages, comparisons and filed answers

The agent

Schema

SCHEMA.md: the rules for structure, naming and tags

You and the agent together

Karpathy’s gist describes the same split and notes the schema can be a file like CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md. In Hermes it’s SCHEMA.md. At the start of every session the agent reads SCHEMA.md, index.md and the last 20 to 30 log entries before it does anything, so it always knows the current state.

The folder structure

```

~/wiki/

SCHEMA.md # rules for the wiki

index.md # map of every page

log.md # append-only history (rotated)

raw/ # articles, papers, transcripts, assets

entities/ # people, companies, tools

concepts/ # ideas and methods

comparisons/ # side-by-side analysis

queries/ # answers worth keeping

```

Raw files carry a little frontmatter — source URL, ingest date and a sha256 hash. If you re-ingest a source that hasn’t changed, the agent skips it; if it has changed, the agent flags the drift.

Ingest, query and lint

Ingest

  • The agent captures the source into raw/ (it can extract web pages and PDFs).
  • It talks through the key takeaways with you (skipped when running on a schedule).
  • It checks what already exists, then writes or updates pages, updates index.md and log.md, and reports the changes.

One source can update 5 to 15 pages. If an ingest would touch 10 or more existing pages, the agent asks first.

Query

  • It reads index.md (and searches once the wiki passes about 100 pages).
  • It reads the relevant pages and writes an answer that cites them with [[wikilinks]].
  • Valuable answers get filed in queries/ or comparisons/ and logged, so the wiki gets smarter from your questions.

Lint

  • Finds orphan pages, broken wikilinks and pages missing from the index.
  • Checks frontmatter, stale pages (over 90 days), contradictions and low-confidence claims.
  • Spots source drift, pages over about 200 lines, messy tags and a log that needs rotating (over 500 entries).
  • Reports issues by severity and logs the run.

The conventions that keep it clean

  • Lowercase, hyphenated filenames.
  • YAML frontmatter on every page: title, created, updated, type, tags and sources, plus optional confidence, contested and contradictions.
  • At least two outbound [[wikilinks]] per page.
  • Provenance markers on pages built from three or more sources.
  • A tag taxonomy of 10 to 20 tags.
  • A page gets created when two or more sources mention something, or it’s central to one.
  • Split pages that grow past about 200 lines, and move retired pages to _archive/.

Obsidian integration and headless sync

The wiki works as an Obsidian vault out of the box: wikilinks are clickable, Graph View shows how everything connects, and the frontmatter powers Dataview queries. Set Obsidian’s attachment folder to raw/assets/. If you also use the obsidian skill, point OBSIDIAN_VAULT_PATH at the same folder as your wiki. Karpathy sums the pairing up neatly: “Obsidian is the IDE; the LLM is the program.”

If Hermes runs on a server, the skill describes syncing with Obsidian Headless. You need Node 22+ and an Obsidian Sync subscription:

```

npm install -g obsidian-headless

ob login

ob sync-create-remote --name "LLM Wiki"

ob sync-setup --vault ""

ob sync --continuous

```

You can run the continuous sync as a systemd user service so it keeps going after you log out. For more on pairing Hermes with Obsidian, see Hermes Obsidian.

LLM Wiki vs RAG

LLM Wiki

RAG

How it works

Compiles sources into a maintained wiki

Searches raw documents at question time

Memory

Rediscovers the answer each time

What you can see

Scale

An index works up to roughly 100 sources and hundreds of pages, per Karpathy

Built for large document sets

RAG is still useful for huge document piles. For a focused research topic you return to again and again, the wiki wins because the work you put in stays done.

Troubleshooting the Hermes LLM wiki

  • The skill is missing. Bundled skills are copied into ~/.hermes/skills/ when you install and synced on hermes update. Restore it with hermes skills reset llm-wiki --restore.
  • The wiki is in the wrong place. Check WIKI_PATH in ~/.hermes/.env; without it the wiki goes to ~/wiki.
  • Answers ignore recent work. Make sure SCHEMA.md, index.md and log.md exist and are up to date — the agent reads them first.
  • Big ingests stall. Ingests touching 10+ pages wait for your approval.
  • You want a batch build. The skill mentions llm-wiki-compiler, a Node.js CLI that compiles a wiki in one pass; use the skill itself when you want the agent curating with you.

My verdict on the Hermes LLM wiki

It’s one of the most useful skills already sitting in your Hermes install. Set WIKI_PATH, run /llm-wiki, feed it a few good sources and lint it once a week, and you end up with a knowledge base that keeps getting better instead of a pile of chats you never read again. If you research anything seriously, set up the Hermes LLM wiki today.

FAQ: hermes llm wiki

What is the Hermes LLM wiki?

A bundled Hermes Agent skill, llm-wiki, that builds and maintains a knowledge base of interlinked markdown pages based on Andrej Karpathy’s LLM Wiki pattern.

Where does Hermes store the wiki?

In the folder set by WIKI_PATH, for example in ~/.hermes/.env. If it isn’t set, the default is ~/wiki.

What are ingest, query and lint?

Ingest adds a source and updates pages, query answers questions from the wiki with citations, and lint health-checks the wiki for broken links, stale pages and contradictions.

Can I use the Hermes LLM wiki with Obsidian?

Yes. The wiki folder works as an Obsidian vault out of the box, with clickable wikilinks, Graph View and Dataview support.

Run hermes skills reset llm-wiki –restore. Bundled skills are also synced when you run hermes update.
